message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for NORTH_CAROLINA_AVENUE.

The current bid is $89. I have $726 cash and own the pink monopoly with four houses each. I am considering raising to $90 or dropping out.

p4 owns the light blue monopoly and two railroads. They are in jail with $763 cash. They own Pennsylvania Avenue, which is mortgaged. This makes them a strong bidder for North Carolina Avenue.

p4 would still need Pacific Avenue from p1 to complete a full green set. I am weighing whether to raise to the $90 minimum bid or drop out, since winning at $150 would let me mortgage North Carolina for cash and block p4 from acquiring a second green.

Mortgaging North Carolina Avenue returns $150, but it cannot generate rent without a full set. This makes the $150 cap risky, since the property would sit idle and lose its strategic value.

p1 is positioned on North Carolina Avenue, suggesting they landed there and declined to buy. No houses remain in the bank, so no one can build right now. p4 wants to complete a green set.

All 32 houses are currently in use. No one can build until someone sells back.

p1's dark blue properties are extremely dangerous. Boardwalk with four houses pays $1700 in rent, and Park Place with three pays $1100. Landing there would force me to sell houses to pay.

I am currently on Pennsylvania Avenue, which p4 owns but is mortgaged, so I avoid rent.

p4 has no get-out-of-jail-free card, so they must pay $50 or roll doubles to exit. They have more cash than me, which makes them a dangerous opponent in this war.

I am weighing whether blocking p4 is worth the $150 cap. If they acquire North Carolina, they would still need Pacific Avenue from p1 to complete a green set. p1 is nearly broke with only $29, so p4 might trade for Pacific.

A green monopoly would be powerful, but all houses are currently locked and no one can build until someone sells back.

I am raising to $90. The pink monopoly pays $750 to $900 in rent, and p1's Boardwalk with four houses is the biggest threat at $1700. I will continue min-raising toward the $150 cap.

I am reconsidering the $150 cap. At $90, winning would net me $60 cash after mortgaging North Carolina. But p4 is matching every bid, so I will not win at $90 unless they drop out. The real value of min-raising is draining p4's cash.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for North Carolina Avenue.

I have $726 and a pink monopoly with 4 houses each. I am on Pennsylvania Avenue and hold one get-out-of-jail card. Player 1 has only $29 and owns dark blues but is cash poor. Player 3 is bankrupt.

Player 4 has $763 and owns light blues with 4 houses, plus railroads. Player 1 dropped out.

The auction for North Carolina Avenue is at $91. I will bid $92 to cap the purchase near $150, mortgage the property, and deny Player 4 a second green. If Player 4 bids higher, I will drop out.

Bidding $92 nets $58 cash after mortgaging. Paying up to $150 would leave me with zero net cash but still block Player 4 from completing a green monopoly, since they need Pacific from Player 1 and an unmortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue.

A green monopoly would not immediately threaten me. With zero houses in the bank, no one can build until properties are sold back. The base rent for North Carolina Avenue is only $20, and even a full monopoly yields just $40.

Player 4 is aggressively matching every bid with $763 in cash while in jail. They want North Carolina Avenue to complete their green set. I am reconsidering whether to raise above the $150 cap, since blocking them from a second green could be strategically valuable beyond mortgage arbitrage. Player 4 might trade with Player 1 for Pacific if they acquire the property.

A completed green monopoly would be devastating once houses are freed. North Carolina with a hotel pays $1,275. Pennsylvania Avenue with a hotel pays $1,400. Pacific Avenue with a hotel pays $1,275.

Player 1's Boardwalk at four houses pays $1,700. Player 1's Park Place at three houses pays $1,100.

I am currently on Player 4's mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue. I pay no rent.

I calculated that selling all twelve houses from my pink monopoly would yield only $600. Combined with my $726 cash, I would have $1,326 total. That is still short of the $1,700 rent on Player 1's Boardwalk at four houses. I would need to mortgage properties to survive such a hit. The four-house rents on St. Charles Place, States Avenue, and Virginia Avenue are $625, $625, and $700 respectively.

Player 4's light blue properties with four houses pay $450, $450, and $600. Player 1 is cash poor and sitting on North Carolina Avenue because they declined to buy it.

Player 1's path from North Carolina Avenue is long and circuitous. They would pass several properties before reaching my pink monopoly, so they are unlikely to land on my houses immediately.

message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for North Carolina Avenue.

I have $726 cash and a fully built pink monopoly. My opponent has very little cash but dangerous dark blue properties. Player three is bankrupt.

Player four has $763 cash and a light blue monopoly. He currently leads the auction at $93 for North Carolina Avenue. I will bid up to about $150, then drop out. If I win under that amount, I will mortgage the property to preserve cash and block his second green.

Mortgaging North Carolina Avenue at $94 would return exactly $150, netting me $56 in cash. This blocks player four from completing a second green monopoly, which he could otherwise trade for with player one.

Player one's dark blue properties are extremely dangerous, but he only has $29 cash. Player four's light blue monopoly yields roughly $1,500 in rent. This makes the North Carolina Avenue bid a clear priority.

I will continue making the minimum $94 raise. This forces player four to pay more if he wins, and it keeps the bid under my $150 cap.
